spots.name: São Pedro do Estoril
spots.notes: The general beach area. Choose Bico or Bafureira for a break-specific estimate. Strong swell shadow: west and south-west swell preferred; exposure falls sharply around 282–290°. This initial local curve needs checking against beach observations, especially on large, long-period swells.

sources.title: Owner comparison with Surfline, 5 September 2026
sources.note: São Pedro is strongly direction-dependent; useful swell around 272°, marginal near 282–283°, usually flat above 290°. Initial curve is a local observation, not a verified universal cutoff. GFS bearings are retained as supplied.

spots.name: São Pedro do Estoril · Bico
spots.notes: Local guidance: works well at low tide; mid tide can work with bigger swell. Rock bottom and access need an instructor assessment. Strong swell shadow: west and south-west swell preferred; exposure falls sharply around 282–290°. This initial local curve needs checking against beach observations, especially on large, long-period swells.

sources.title: Owner observations, 5 September 2026
sources.note: Bico: low tide, mid tide with bigger swell. Bafureira: mid-high tide with higher swell.

sources.title: Owner comparison with Surfline, 5 September 2026
sources.note: São Pedro is strongly direction-dependent; useful swell around 272°, marginal near 282–283°, usually flat above 290°. Initial curve is a local observation, not a verified universal cutoff. GFS bearings are retained as supplied.

spots.name: São Pedro do Estoril · Bafureira
spots.notes: Local guidance: favours mid to high tide with higher swell. Published school guidance also identifies mid tide. Rocky bottom. Strong swell shadow: west and south-west swell preferred; exposure falls sharply around 282–290°. This initial local curve needs checking against beach observations, especially on large, long-period swells.

sources.note: Bico: low tide, mid tide with bigger swell. Bafureira: mid-high tide with higher swell.

spots.name: Carcavelos
spots.notes: South-southwest exposure. North winds are offshore; banks and crowding change which part of the beach works.

spots.name: Guincho
spots.notes: Exposed beach with strong local wind effects. Mid to low tide is an initial preference; sandbanks vary.

spots.name: Cresmina
spots.notes: Nearby Guincho conditions provide the initial reference. Local shelter and sandbanks still need calibration.

spots.name: Abano
spots.notes: Small beach north of Guincho. Initial exposure settings need observations at the actual lesson area.

spots.name: Parede
spots.notes: Point break with a rocky bottom and potentially long paddle. Initial preference is mid tide.

spots.name: Tamariz
spots.notes: Sheltered south-facing beach. Numerical settings are provisional; confirm the chosen peak and access locally.

spots.name: Praia Grande
spots.notes: Exposed Atlantic beach. Mid tide is an initial preference; conditions depend on sandbanks. Northern-wind shelter varies along the beach.

spots.name: Praia Pequena
spots.notes: Smaller beach north of Praia Grande, with some northern-wind shelter. Observe the banks and rocks before a lesson.

spots.name: Adraga
spots.notes: Open Atlantic exposure, cliffs and rocks. Mid-tide weighting is an initial assumption, not a measured calibration.

spots.name: Praia das Maçãs
spots.notes: Beach at the river mouth. Sandbanks and local currents can change; initial settings need instructor observations.

spots.name: Magoito
spots.notes: Exposed coast beneath cliffs. Initial wave and tide settings require local calibration.

spots.name: São Julião
spots.notes: Open-coast beach at the Sintra and Mafra boundary. Initial settings need confirmation for the selected banks.

spots.name: Praia de São João · Caparica
spots.notes: Sandy beach near the Tagus mouth. Banks, currents and shelter vary along the beach; mid-tide preference is provisional.

spots.name: Praia da Cornélia · Caparica
spots.notes: Southern part of Praia da Saúde, known as Cornélia. Initial settings represent a sandy west-facing beach and need local observations.
